summary: HID sensor daemon corruption prevents user profile load after resume on several laptop models
description:
Issue summary:
Several recently depot-repaired laptops are hitting a consistent failure to load the Windows user profile after resuming from S3 (suspend). Machines appear to boot, login occurs at the credential prompt, but user profile services fail to mount and the session loops back to the sign-in screen.

Impact:
- Affected internal users cannot access their desktop after depot repair or battery replacement; productivity is blocked until a technician visits.
- Roughly ~8 confirmed devices across two models so far; potential wider exposure from recent OEM driver bundle updated in depot image.

Environment:
- Redeployed corporate image (CorpImage-2026-02-18) via SCCM task sequence at depot.
- OS: Windows 11 23H2, corp image with custom drivers.
- Regions: us-east and eu-west depots.

Steps to reproduce (observed reliably):
1) Depot tech performs battery replacement and reimaging with CorpImage-2026-02-18 via SCCM.
2) Device boots, device drivers and agent bundles install during OOBE.
3) Technician signs in to validate provisioning, then places machine to sleep (S3) for QA transport.
4) On resume, user signs in; profile load fails, explorer does not start, and sign-in returns to lock screen.

Observed behavior:
- Event Viewer: repeated errors from "User Profile Service" (Event ID 1530) with path access issues referencing C:\Users\<username> tmp symlinks.
- Windows logs show multiple crash dumps from a process named redwood-hid-daemon.exe around resume time.
- Device manager shows HID-compliant device with warning immediately after resume.

Expected behavior:
- Normal resume with user profile loading, explorer starting, and endpoint agents initializing.

Workaround in place:
- Remote assistance to create a new local admin profile and migrate data; not ideal.
- Temporary mitigation: instruct depot techs to avoid putting device to sleep during post-repair QA (hold on login and run a scripted sleep/resume test locally instead of S3) and to roll back to previous driver package for HID devices when possible.
investigation_notes:
Telemetry and early hypotheses:
- Repro on two different hardware models suggests common software component.
- redwood-hid-daemon.exe (our in-house HID sensor agent included in the corp image) shows an unhandled exception during resume sequence; stack traces point at descriptor parsing after EC/ACPI wake.
- Core dump (collected from one device) shows heap corruption pattern following a call to HidParseDescriptor() shipped by vendor-hidkit.dll included in driver package v1.4.3 (added to depot bundle 2026-02-10).
- Correlation: all affected devices were imaged after 2026-02-10, which matches when vendor-hidkit.dll v1.4.3 was added to the depot bundle.

Actions taken so far:
- Collected dumps from 3 devices and uploaded to SRE/Platform storage (link in comments).
- Re-imaged a test Dell Latitude 7440 with previous driver bundle (v1.4.1) — resume succeeds and profile loads as expected.
- Reproduced failure on an isolated lab machine using CorpImage-2026-02-18 and driver bundle v1.4.3.
- Eng assigned to reproduce in VM with kernel debug; initial test shows same crash sequence.

Hypothesis:
- Vendor HID library v1.4.3 contains an incompatible change that triggers heap corruption when redwood-hid-daemon parses certain descriptor sequences after S3 resume, causing the agent to crash and leave temporary profile symlinks in a bad state, resulting in User Profile Service errors.

Next steps:
- SRE/Platform to prepare an emergency rollback of vendor-hidkit.dll to v1.4.1 in depot image artifact (blocked by QA signoff).
- Dev (Marcus) to add defensive parsing and crash handling in redwood-hid-daemon; publish hotfix build for validation.
- Depot leads to pause issuance of CorpImage-2026-02-18 until rollback or hotfix is validated.
- Create follow-up change to add resume smoke test to depot QA checklist.

resolution_notes:
Mitigation applied: Depot teams instructed to use driver bundle v1.4.1 for immediate repairs and to avoid sleep during post-repair QA. Hotfix for redwood-hid-daemon (with defensive parsing and crash handling) built and delivered to internal QA on 2026-03-14.

Planned permanent fix:
- Release hotfix agent v2.3.1 and update CorpImage with either the fixed agent or vendor driver rollback after validation.
- Add resume/suspend smoke test to depot SCCM task sequence and QA checklist to catch regressions.
- Open follow-up change request to vendor to investigate descriptor parsing differences between v1.4.1 and v1.4.3.

Follow-ups created:
- INT-386421 (Task): Update depot SCCM task sequence to include resume smoke test.
- INT-386422 (Bug): Vendor driver compatibility verification and coordination.
resolution: Mitigated - workarounds deployed; permanent fix pending hotfix validation
